name: Carbon monoxide (CO)
what_it_does: When inhaled, it reduces the amount of oxygen the blood can carry.
air_pollution_impact: Incomplete burning of fuel releases CO. In sunlight, it can participate in reactions that produce ground-level ozone.

name: Nitrogen monoxide (NO)
what_it_does: It reacts with ozone in the air to form nitrogen dioxide.
air_pollution_impact: Engines and other high-temperature combustion sources release NO. Its conversion to nitrogen dioxide feeds the chemistry that produces smog.

name: Nitrogen dioxide (NO₂)
what_it_does: It irritates the airways and can worsen asthma symptoms.
air_pollution_impact: Sunlight breaks down NO₂ in a reaction that leads to ozone formation. Other reactions produce nitrate particles that add to fine particle pollution.

name: Ground-level ozone (O₃)
what_it_does: It irritates the lungs and can damage plant leaves.
air_pollution_impact: It forms when nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds react in sunlight. It is a major component of smog.

name: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂)
what_it_does: It can narrow the airways and make breathing difficult, especially for people with asthma.
air_pollution_impact: Burning sulfur-containing fuels releases SO₂. In the atmosphere it can form sulfate particles and contribute to acid rain.

name: Fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅)
what_it_does: Particles up to 2.5 micrometers across can reach deep into the lungs. Exposure can harm the heart and lungs.
air_pollution_impact: Smoke and soot add fine particles directly. Reactions between gases also create fine particles, which can build up and reduce visibility.

name: Inhalable particulate matter (PM₁₀)
what_it_does: Particles up to 10 micrometers across can enter the respiratory tract and aggravate breathing problems.
air_pollution_impact: Road dust, construction, and windblown soil add inhalable particles to the air. PM₁₀ includes the smaller PM₂.₅ particles as well.

name: Ammonia (NH₃)
what_it_does: At high concentrations, this gas irritates the eyes, nose, and throat.
air_pollution_impact: Ammonia released from manure and fertilizers reacts with acids in the air to form fine particles such as ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulfate.
